subject: Latest spOccupancy package now with added multi-season functionality

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Latest spOccupancy package now with added multi-season functionality
parts:
Dear all,

 

in the latest version of the spOccupancy package on CRAN, Jeff Doser has added functionality for spatio-temporal occupancy models – these are the functions tPGOcc() and stPGOcc(), see the new vignette on the package website here. Both functions are based on the same technology as the rest of the package: Polya-Gamma data augmentation to deal with (very) large data sets and nearest-neighbour Gaussian processes (NNGPs) for dealing with spatial dependence. But now you can also model open, or multi-season, data sets. This is typically when you have data collected for more than a year for birds or perhaps for more than a week for insects. The current implementations of these models are not dynamic, but rather stratify the parameters by season and then model space- or space- and time-dependence using GPs and/or AR(1) processes. Conceptually, these new models are analogous to those in Rushing et al. (2019), Diana et al. (2021), Hepler and Erhardt (2021) and also some work by Allan Clark and Res Altwegg at UCT.

 

One of the cool things about the new functions is that they accept single-visit (SV) data. Spatial and temporal autocorrelation creates a sort of "fractional" replication that enables parameter estimates in occupancy models also in the SV case. (Note: This is the usual explanation for why a Dail-Madsen (or dynamic N-mixture) model often "works" with SV data.) So, provided there is sufficient spatial and/or temporal structure in your data, these new functions should enable you to model occupancy and detection separately even in the SV case. This should greatly expand the range of cases where species distribution modelling with an explicit treatment of the false-negative observation process becomes possible.

 

Best regards  --- Marc
